name: miu
use_label: Open very large text files fast
one_liner: A minimal text editor that opens very large files instantly and draws colour emoji.

text.why: Past a few hundred megabytes, most editors stall on open. miu maps the file instead of loading it whole, so a large file opens straight away, and being written directly against C++ and Win32 keeps it light.
text.take: It spends its effort on opening fast and not freezing rather than on features — a difference you feel immediately if you read logs for a living.
build: Text and colour emoji are rendered with DirectWrite. It has regular-expression search and replace with case and whole-word options, multiple cursors, rectangular selection, unlimited undo, a dark mode and F1 help, and uses Google’s compact_enc_det to detect encodings. Built binaries are on GitHub Releases.

who.role: People who open big logs and data files often, and Windows users after a lighter Notepad.

start.text: Download the binary from GitHub Releases and run it — there is no install step.

caveat: The documentation is Japanese-first. It is built primarily for Windows (the repository also lists macOS and iOS targets), and building it yourself means preparing the encoding-detection library first.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
